summary: A first-person action passage from Book 6, part 36, in which the narrator throws a flaming bottle back at attackers, triggering an explosion that sets the van and several men on fire. The narrator is wounded by the blast, shoots the surviving attackers in the legs to hit their arteries, and tallies the dead while wondering whether more enemies remain. The text is a fragment that ends mid-scene as the narrator considers whether gunmen are still aiming at the van.
one_line: A first-person combat fragment from Book 6 where the narrator returns a firebomb, sets attackers ablaze, and shoots the survivors.
key_facts: The narrator swings the bottle around in a circle and smacks it with the heel of the hand before letting it fly back the other way.
The flame from the bottle blisters the narrator's hand.
The narrator's sleeve catches fire and the narrator smothers it against their body while ducking.
The narrator calculates the bottle's landing time using the math of free fall: height of zero, solve for time.
The explosion is too loud for the narrator to hear the bottle shatter.
The napalm splatters against the van's metal, and the flames lick above the van's roof.
The narrator's hearing rings out into complete silence for an instant before returning.
The narrator rolls under the van and retrieves a Colt pistol.
The narrator shoots the surviving attackers in the legs and aims for the arteries rather than shooting to wound.
The narrator has counted six burning bodies on the ground and shot three more.
The narrator's running tally is ten dead, counting the one killed in the SUV.
The narrator questions whether the attackers would really have sent more than twelve men.
The passage ends with the narrator speculating that remaining attackers have their sights set on the van, ready to shoot the narrator.
